The team proposes Repeatable Read because a stable snapshot and absence of phantom rows should make the combined decisions equivalent to serial execution. If a transaction fails for a serialization reason, the proposed recovery retries only the failed SQL statement, expecting PostgreSQL to replay the earlier decision logic automatically. A generic retry wrapper would also retry every unique-key violation without inspecting its cause.

Also, note correction of premise: "Repeatable Read ... should make combined decisions equivalent to serial execution" — false; documented that RR prevents phantom reads in PG (stronger than standard minimum, which allows phantoms), but RR permits serialization anomalies; applevel-consistency says integrity checks can fail due to read/write conflicts; attempts to enforce business rules at RR are not likely to work without explicit locks. Recovery premise: retry only the failed statement — wrong. Docs: retry complete transaction including logic deciding which SQL/values; PostgreSQL offers no automatic retry. Also on error, transaction is aborted; in RR, "could not serialize access due to concurrent update" rolls back the transaction. After a serialization failure in PostgreSQL, the transaction is aborted and must be rolled back; the failed statement retry inside the same aborted transaction will fail with "current transaction is aborted". Can I cite that? The transaction-iso page says "the repeatable read transaction will be rolled back" and "abort the current transaction and retry the whole transaction from the beginning."
